knowledge_point.title: Identifying an Invertible Function From Its Graph

question.:question/problem:
![](images/86/86789a860ad2ca40419dbf47bb2939865e42c3316f162d07abace5f2efe9a05d.png)

Which of the graphs above correspond to an invertible function?

Each graph shows its entire domain; an open circle excludes its endpoint.

Select all that apply.

Graph positions: **I.** upper left; **II.** upper right; **III.** lower left; **IV.** lower right.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A function is invertible if and only if it's a one-to-one function. To determine which of the functions are one-to-one, we use the horizontal line test.

![](images/45/450a431d00c33e12a60cf22d1e108c6147c6fa1ed0276068879e7d6008ea843e.png)

From the above, we see that:

- For graphs II, IV, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line. Therefore, these graphs show one-to-one functions. As a result, these functions are invertible.

- For graphs I, III, some horizontal lines intersect the curve more than once. These are not one-to-one functions. As a result, they are not invertible.
